clue.text: Huge pile of cash, unused

blocks.note: first meaning: a vast sum of money, as in 'it cost a fortune'
second meaning: in pristine, as-new condition, as a collector would say

explanation.walkthrough: The comma makes it read as a hoard of money nobody has spent; the two halves are separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both slang for an enormous fortune and the collector's term for something in perfect, never-handled condition.

clue.text: Break part of arm, did you say?

indicators.note: asking whether you said something points to a word heard rather than read, so the spelling changes

blocks.note: the breech is the rear part of a gun barrel, and a gun is a firearm, or arm

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether you said you broke a bone in your arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arm' looks like the limb, but here it means a weapon, so the part is the breech of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A breach is a gap, rupture or violation, so it is a synonym of break as a noun.

clue.text: Cry from attention-seeker stuck in maze, youngster going the wrong way

indicators.note: something stuck in other words sits inside them, so the letters run across the words maze and youngster
going the wrong way means travelling backwards, so the hidden run is read right to left

blocks.note: the end of maze and the start of youngster

explanation.surface: A child lost in a maze shouts for help and heads off in the wrong direction.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is read backwards: ZEYO turned round is OYEZ.
explanation.definitionFit: A town crier traditionally calls 'oyez' three times to gain the crowd's attention before an announcement.

clue.text: Bulb glowing and radiating light is coruscating, first of all

indicators.note: the first of all the words means taking the opening letter of each word in the run

blocks.clueFragment: glowing and radiating light is coruscating
blocks.note: opening letters of the six words

explanation.surface: A description of a light bulb shining brilliantly.
explanation.walkthrough: Bulb points at a lamp, and the glowing words keep that picture going, but the bulb is a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant grows as a bulb of cloves used in cooking, so the bulb names it by its form.

clue.text: Book hour hosted by ship’s guide

indicators.note: a guest hosted by someone is taken in by them, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: HR is the standard abbreviation for hour
the tiller is the bar used to steer a boat

explanation.surface: Someone reserves an hour with a navigator aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb meaning reserve, but it is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A thriller is a kind of novel full of suspense, so it is an example of a book.

clue.text: Sweet thing right to invest in crooked game?

indicators.note: to invest something in a thing is to put it inside, so the abbreviation goes into the next word

blocks.note: R is the usual abbreviation for right
bandy means bent outwards, as in bandy legs
Snap is a card game where players shout when two cards match

explanation.surface: Is it a good idea to put money into a rigged game?
explanation.walkthrough: Bandy legs are bowed outwards, which is why bandy can mean crooked; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A brandy snap is a crisp rolled ginger biscuit, often filled with cream, so it is a confection.

clue.text: One drink like another? Two can play at that game!

definitions.text: Two can play at that game!

blocks.note: gin is a spirit
rum is another spirit, and adding -y makes an adjective meaning resembling it

explanation.surface: One drink tastes like another, and the reply quotes the saying about retaliation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two can play at that game' is a stock retort, but here it literally describes a card game for two players.
explanation.definitionFit: Gin rummy is a card game usually played by exactly two people, so the idiom describes it literally.

clue.text: Scrambled brain? I’m cooler

indicators.note: scrambled things are mixed up, like eggs, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone with a muddled mind insists they are the calm one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' reads as calmer, but it is the noun: something that keeps things cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A minibar is the small refrigerator of drinks in a hotel room, so it is a kind of cooler.

clue.text: On the beach remains source of metal

blocks.note: ash is what remains after burning
ore is rock that metal is extracted from

explanation.surface: Something washed up on the beach turns out to hold metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on land rather than at sea, as on a beach, so the phrase is an equivalent.

clue.text: Breed anxiety

blocks.note: first meaning: a variety of plant, animal or microbe
second meaning: tension, pressure or stress

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a particular variety within a species and also the mental tension caused by pressure.

clue.text: Braless predators of South America? Huge number!

indicators.note: less means without, so the three letters spelling bra are dropped from what follows

blocks.note: Brazil is the largest country of South America
lions are big hunting cats

explanation.surface: A joking question about uncovered big cats in the Amazon, followed by a cry of amazement.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAZIL LIONS without BRA leaves ZIL LIONS; 'Braless' looks like a description, but it is the deletion instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Zillions is an informal term for an indefinitely vast quantity, so it names a huge number.

clue.text: As here, initial letters ordered so?

definitions.text: As here, initial letters ordered so?

blocks.clueFragment: As here, initial letters ordered so?
blocks.note: surface reading: a question about how the first letters of something are arranged
setter's reading: take the first letter of each word of the clue, A, H, I, L, O, S, and they run in dictionary order

explanation.walkthrough: The clue describes itself: its own initial letters run A, H, I, L, O, S, which is the order the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes things arranged from A to Z, which is how the clue's initials happen to fall.

clue.text: Hero in England, I’m a maverick

indicators.note: a maverick refuses to follow the usual line, so the letters break from their order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An English rebel proclaims themselves a hero.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero of a play or film is the principal male role, so the actor playing him has the top part.

clue.text: Reversible doctrine?

indicators.note: something reversible works the same either way round, so the word reads identically backwards

blocks.note: a principle held as true, and the word reads the same in both directions

explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversible' sounds like a belief that can be overturned, but it describes the spelling of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or belief held by a group, which is what a doctrine is.

clue.text: Statistics collected together, a bit taken aback

indicators.note: taken aback suggests being knocked backwards, so the pieces are read in the other direction

blocks.note: taken as written
a tad is a small amount

explanation.surface: Someone is slightly surprised by gathered figures.
explanation.walkthrough: A TAD reversed gives the answer; 'taken aback' looks like surprise, but it turns the letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and figures gathered for analysis, which is what collected statistics are.

clue.text: Exploding, no star is lighter!

indicators.note: something exploding is blown apart, so the letters scatter and land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cosmic boast: no exploding star gives off more light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' looks like a comparison of brightness or weight, but it means one who lights fires.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsonist deliberately sets fires, so is someone who lights things, a lighter in the cryptic sense.

clue.text: With narrowest of leads in cricket match, build hastily

definitions.text: With narrowest of leads in cricket match

blocks.clueFragment: With narrowest of leads in cricket match
blocks.note: first meaning: one run ahead, the smallest possible margin in cricket, where scores are counted in runs
second meaning: to make something quickly, as with a dress or a shed

explanation.surface: A team clinging to a tiny lead throws something together in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the score is counted in runs, so a side just one ahead is a run up.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to make or sew something quickly, and the phrase also states a one-point margin.

clue.text: God fastens underwear

blocks.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
ties means binds or fastens

explanation.surface: A deity is pictured securing his undergarments.
explanation.definitionFit: Panties are women's knickers, so they are a type of underwear garment.

clue.text: Telephone cartel

blocks.note: first meaning: to call someone, as a verb
second meaning: a group combining to fix prices or rig deals

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means making a phone call, and the noun is a gang or syndicate acting together illegally.

clue.text: Engineer putting in a seal, strip of sticky material

indicators.note: to engineer something is to construct or contrive it, so the letters are built into something new

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An engineer seals a joint with adhesive strip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' reads as the person doing the job, but it is a verb telling you to rebuild the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the adhesive plastic tape electricians wrap round wires, so it is a sticky strip.

clue.text: Pioneering surgeon one catalogues, might you say?

blocks.note: first meaning: Joseph ..., the British surgeon who introduced antiseptic surgery
second meaning: someone who makes lists, a whimsical coinage the question mark owns up to

explanation.walkthrough: The question 'might you say?' admits the second meaning is an invented word rather than a dictionary entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Lister pioneered antiseptic surgery, and a person who compiles lists could jokingly be called by his surname.

clue.text: Sunbed, possibly, in old money

blocks.note: first meaning: something that tans you, of which a sunbed is one example
second meaning: a sixpence, a coin of Britain's pre-decimal currency

explanation.surface: A tanning bed is paid for with pre-decimal coins.
explanation.walkthrough: Old money is British slang for the pounds, shillings and pence used before 1971; a tanner was the sixpenny coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything that bronzes skin is literally a tanner, and the word was also slang for a sixpence coin.

clue.text: Swimming in sea, dog was distressed

indicators.note: swimming letters are moving about loosely, so they settle in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dog out of its depth in the sea is in a state.
explanation.definitionFit: To agonise is to worry or suffer intensely, so the past tense matches being upset.

clue.text: Channel avoided, reportedly?

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by speech, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: ducked means dodged or avoided

explanation.surface: A broadcaster apparently steered clear of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' reads as a TV station, but it means a tube or conduit.
explanation.definitionFit: A duct is a tube or passage carrying air or fluid, which is a kind of channel.

clue.text: Deliberately miss Italian title, having thrown away lead

indicators.note: throwing away the lead means losing what comes first, so the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: Signore is the Italian equivalent of Mr or sir

explanation.surface: An Italian nobleman squanders his advantage and misses on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore something is to pay no attention to it on purpose, so you intentionally overlook it.

clue.text: Free to defend a surprise attack

indicators.note: to defend something is to surround and protect it, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: to rid is to free of something
taken as written

explanation.surface: Freedom fighters are urged to protect themselves from an ambush.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside RID: R-A-ID.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid is a sudden incursion on a place by police or soldiers, so it is an unexpected assault.

clue.text: Female twit in fiction

blocks.note: first meaning: a girl or young woman, chiefly in Scottish use
second meaning: points at the famous collie of novels and films, though the clue's wording is odd here

explanation.walkthrough: Lassie is the heroic collie of the novel and films 'Lassie Come Home'; 'twit' fits her poorly and may be a misprint.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is Scots for a girl, and it is also the name of a famous fictional dog, herself female.

clue.text: Superficial wound comes with it, first of cuts

indicators.note: read as the past of wind, wound means twisted round, so the letters are coiled into a new order
the first of a word is its opening letter alone

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A shallow wound is the first of many cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' reads as an injury, but it is the past tense of wind, signalling twisting.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic change affects only the outward appearance, not the substance, so it is skin-deep.
